commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 14 (vegetable plaiting materials) derived entry_is_line_a..e from five out-of-chapter HTS statistical reporting numbers with proof atoms citing other chapters' provisions, so the trade-action components gated on those flags rested on conditions with no basis in this chapter's cited source.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 12; diff read individually and normalized-compared against index 12 — the only differences are cosmetic generator placement variation (temporal key spelled `effective_from` instead of `from`), no substantive difference. Same caveats as index 12 (boilerplate 'runtime semantics are unchanged' summary line, referencing formulas re-gated in a sibling commit of PR #1300, exemplar citation paths left in source_verification).
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical or as mere refactoring and could not: the ch14 diff deletes five `kind: derived` rules whose formulas were `hts_number == "<line>"` for five HTS statistical reporting numbers that belong to chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95, each with proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, and converts the identifiers into caller inputs — a change to the module's rule set and input surface, not to hashes, pins or formatting. Inside a chapter-14 composition those equalities can never hold for a chapter-14 entry, so every consumer branch built on them was dead: `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate` never fired for any chapter-14 line, and `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (source: "Chapter 99 U.S. note reciprocal annex exclusion list under heading 9903.01.32") got its truth value from a ferroalloy line rather than from the annex list. That is a branch grounded on the wrong provision, which the task's taxonomy places squarely under untraceable_branch, and the fix removes it; wrong_entity_or_scope is the only serious runner-up and fits less well because what changed is the branch's source grounding, not the declared entity or population.
triage.verifier_notes: Staging caveat (main reason I stopped short of high confidence): in THIS commit the ch14 consumer formulas are byte-identical pre/post — `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`, the five §301 slots, the §338 beer slot all survive unchanged (pre lines 2467/2672/3094 == post 2367/2572/2994). Only the five derivations are deleted, so the module stops asserting a groundless condition but the membership-semantic replacement (and the a/b/d retention, c/e replacement noted in the PR's issue comment) lands in later commits of PR #1300. Root cause is generator-side: tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py in this same commit adds `selected.difference_update(ENTRY_FLAG_RULES)` with the comment "generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars" (generator source, not the module diff). Corpus check through the pinned release: the 9903.01.32 annex exclusion list (us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-178..180) jumps 1207.91.00 → 1521.10.00 with no chapter-13 or chapter-14 subheadings, so for that one consumer rule the pre-fix always-false answer was accidentally correct; the load-bearing wrongness is the §301/§232 slots being unreachable for every chapter-14 line, consistent with the PR body's "the un-encoded line-list layer drops from 6.58pp to 0.92pp of the window mean". The identical change lands in all 100 generated chapter modules in this commit — a reviewer should dedupe to one representative chapter rather than counting 100 defects. The file is a rulespec/v1 module with rules, versions and proof atoms (module.kind: composition), so not_a_rule_module does not apply.
